label: Morning Brief
periodStart: Wed, Nov 25, 2026, 4:00 PM ET (previous close; markets closed Thursday for Thanksgiving)
timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary. This morning's overnight news and filings snapshot was not available for this run, so coverage runs through about 10:00 PM ET on Nov 26; items already reported in the Nov 26 brief are not repeated.

driver.text: Per Bloomberg, Asian stocks rose for a second day along with US equity-index futures, extending a tentative recovery after weeks of volatility in the AI trade, while Treasuries declined as cash trading resumed (Nov 26, 4:59 PM ET); WSJ said Asian markets were mostly higher as sentiment around AI stabilized (9:13 PM ET). On Thursday WSJ reported U.S. stock futures traded higher, helped by an upward revision to third-quarter GDP (8:01 AM ET), and that Asian investors shrugged off new U.S. tariff proposals (12:22 AM ET). The Financial Times reported a hawkish Fed is poised to raise rates despite the stock market turmoil, with inflation the top concern for officials (9:58 AM ET). In chips, WSJ reported Washington closed a loophole that let Chinese companies access Nvidia chips (7:42 AM ET), and Bloomberg said the Dutch government will resist proposed US curbs on ASML's sales to China (7:23 AM ET). Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

cryptoDriver.text: Per The Block, spot bitcoin ETFs have already hit record monthly net outflows of $5.39 billion in November, with several trading days remaining, putting them on track for their worst month on record. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

calendar.text: About $7 billion of bitcoin options expire Friday (per CoinDesk headline).
